title: http2: do not let a rate limit enlarge the stream window
body:
With a download rate limit, `cf_h2_get_desired_local_win()` uses the rate limiter's available bytes as the HTTP/2 stream window whenever they fit in an int32. A high limit therefore gives a much larger window (up to ~2 GB instead of `H2_STREAM_WINDOW_SIZE_MAX`, 10 MiB).

With `--limit-rate` between ~1024M and 2047M this breaks the transfer: the window update exceeds the HTTP/2 maximum window size and nghttp2 rejects it, so the download fails immediately:
```
  $ curl --http2-prior-knowledge --limit-rate 1500M http://localhost:18443/big.bin -o /dev/null
  [1] nghttp2_submit_window_update() failed: Flow control error(-524)
```
At most 1000M works because the resulting window still fits, and at least 2048M works because the available bytes no longer fit an int32 and the default window is used.

This caps the rate-limited window at `H2_STREAM_WINDOW_SIZE_MAX`, so a rate limit can only reduce the window. Downloads at 1100M, 1500M, and 2047M now complete, and lower limits (5M to 100M) behave as before.
Test 1717 does an HTTP/2 GET with `--limit-rate 1500M` and fails without the change.

Side note: `cf_h2_update_local_win()` calls both `nghttp2_session_set_local_window_size()` and
`nghttp2_submit_window_update()` when growing the window, which raises it twice; that is why ~1 GB is already enough to overflow.
I left that unchanged since curl handles window updates manually.

Tested with nghttp2 1.40.0.

This issue was found by an LLM-Enhanced Static Analysis Engine and verified manually.

files.patch:
@@ -46,8 +46,10 @@ http/2
 <name>
 HTTP/2 GET with Upgrade:
 </name>
+# A rate limit above 1 GB/s must not grow the stream window beyond the
+# HTTP/2 maximum
 <command>
-http://%HOSTIP:%HTTP2PORT/%TESTNUMBER --http2 http://%HOSTIP:%HTTP2PORT/%TESTNUMBER0001
+http://%HOSTIP:%HTTP2PORT/%TESTNUMBER --http2 http://%HOSTIP:%HTTP2PORT/%TESTNUMBER0001 --limit-rate 1500M
 </command>
 </client>
